most_likely: Acute on chronic diastolic (HFpEF) congestive heart failure exacerbation
summary: An elderly obese woman with HFpEF (diastolic CHF, EF>55%), paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, sick sinus syndrome s/p dual-lead pacemaker, myasthenia gravis, seizure disorder and dementia presents days after discharge with severe dyspnea, orthopnea, JVP to the earlobe, 4+ lower extremity/sacral edema, crackles, and CXR showing pulmonary edema with bilateral pleural effusions. ProBNP 4640, troponin negative, TTE with preserved EF>55%, dilated RA/RV, RAP ≥15 mmHg and mild pulmonary hypertension. She required BiPAP in the CCU, was diuresed with IV Lasix then torsemide (weight 116.4 → 108.1 kg), with rising creatinine to 1.6 (baseline 1.1) consistent with cardiorenal acute kidney injury; myasthenia and myoclonic jerks were evaluated by neurology and EEG showed no seizures.
